Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

oneself pronoun

also by oneself, with oneself

classical

Cic. Sen. 49: sēcum esse sēcumque … vīvere
Cic. Off. 2.64: paulum nōn numquam dē suō jūre dēcēdere

suī, sibi, sē (sēsē)

pronoun, reflexive: genitive suī, dative sibi, accusative and ablative sē; the same for every gender and number

oneself, referring to a general subject

With an infinitive or a general subject (quisque, “everyone”) the reflexive is the same sē, and the possessive suus: sēcum vīvere, to live with oneself; dē suō jūre dēcēdere, to give up some of one’s rights.

Other words

  • ipse, ipsa, ipsum — oneself (for emphasis)

    pronoun, intensive · also used · classical

    As in “to do it oneself”: sē ipsum fēlīcem facit.

Examples

  • sēcum esse sēcumque, ut dīcitur, vīvere

    to be with oneself and, as they say, to live with oneselfCic. Sen. 49

  • est enim nōn modo līberāle paulum nōn numquam dē suō jūre dēcēdere, sed interdum etiam frūctuōsum

    For it is not only generous now and then to give up a little of one’s rights, but sometimes profitable too.Cic. Off. 2.64

  • Quod quisque amat, laudandō commendat sibi.

    What one loves, one makes dearer to oneself by praising it.Publ. Q 80

  • suō enim quisque studiō maximē dūcitur

    For each of us is led most by his own interest.Cic. Fin. 5.5

See also one, himself, myself, own.

SourcesLewis & Short: sui · Lewis & Short: ipse
